 8th Pay Commission: Railways Seek More Talks, Defence Staff Demand Higher Pay
 BW Online Bureau
 Nov 18, 2026
 # 8th Pay Commission
 # Indian Railways Employees
 # All India Railwaymen's Federation
 # AIDEF
 # Defence Civilian Employees
 # Minimum Pay
 # Fitment Factor
 # Old Pension Scheme
 # Salary Revision
 # Governme
 Railway employees seek two additional days for consultations, while defence civilian staff demand Rs 69,000 minimum pay and restoration of OPS
 The All India Railwaymen's Federation (AIRF) has sought two additional days of discussions with the 8th Central Pay Commission to present the demands of various categories of railway employees. Separately, the All India Defence Employees' Federation (AIDEF) is scheduled to meet the commission on November 18 to press for higher minimum pay, improved benefits and pension reforms.
 In a letter dated November 12, AIRF General Secretary Shiva Gopal Mishra requested additional time with commission chairperson Ranjana Prakash Desai, arguing that several employee categories have yet to present their specific service-related concerns.
 The federation has sought representation for non-gazetted medical and traffic staff, technical supervisors, ministerial employees, accounts personnel and workers associated with Metro Railway Kolkata, the Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO) and other specialised units.
 AIRF has already submitted its memorandum and held discussions with the commission, most recently on October 31. It said the additional consultations would ensure that the concerns of a wider section of the railway workforce receive consideration.
 Meanwhile, AIDEF, which represents around 50,000 civilian defence employees, plans to demand a minimum basic pay of Rs 69,000 based on a fitment factor of 3.83, calculated using a five-member family unit.
 Other key demands include at least five promotions or assured career progression benefits over 30 years of service, a monthly risk and hardship allowance of Rs 10,000 and higher group insurance coverage. The federation has also sought Rs 2 crore in compensation for employees killed in accidents while on duty.
 On pension reforms, AIDEF has called for the withdrawal of the National Pension System (NPS) and Unified Pension Scheme (UPS), restoration of the Old Pension Scheme (OPS), and revision of pensions for those who retired before January 1, 2026.
 The consultations come as the 8th Pay Commission reviews salary structures, allowances and pension benefits for central government employees and pensioners. Its recommendations are expected to have a significant impact on the compensation and retirement benefits of millions of beneficiaries.
